plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large golden-yellow flower heads that track the sun when young. Widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornamental use, and also found growing wild in prairies and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide in temperate regions including the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower forming dense plumes of tiny golden flowers atop tall stems. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators preparing for autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to meadows, fields, and roadsides of eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects; ragweed blooming at the same time is the real culprit.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like pink-lilac blooms in early autumn with no leaves present. The strap-like foliage appears the following spring and dies back by early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (late August to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe, from the British Isles to central and southern Europe; grown in gardens in temperate zones worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is used medicinally to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem, a small evergreen tree covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pom-pom flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, early September is the start of the wattle blooming peak as winter ends.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, New South Wales, and the Australian Capital Territory
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, marking the start of spring, and the golden and green colors of Australia's sporting teams were inspired by wattle.
